name: Greta
looks: the stern girl in a bright pink blouse with one long braid
occupation: young climate campaigner, a parody of Greta Thunberg
background: Greta left school to walk the border road with a satchel of pamphlets and one question for every grown-up she meets: what are you going to do about it? She has already lectured two kings, a bishop and a mule driver, and she does not count any of them as converted.
temperament: Earnest, stubborn and impossible to flatter; furious at excuses and ready to say so to anyone, however grand, but quietly loyal to those who keep their word.
speech: Short, blunt and accusing, with a cold stare to match; repeats 'how dare you' when angered and asks what you have actually done.
quirks: Points a finger at whoever she is scolding; counts the logs on the fire and tuts; refuses a second helping of anything that was carried a long way; tugs her braid when she is thinking.
secret: She is secretly terrified that nobody is listening, and has never once been able to stop talking in case they stop.
goal: Make every guest in the room admit what they have done wrong, and get at least one person to promise to change.
persona: A stern, unsmiling young campaigner who treats the tavern as a courtroom. No small talk: she asks what you have actually done, points, and waits for an answer, and she picks a new charge for each person (the logs on the fire, ale carted over the pass, the wasted bread, the tower of a tycoon). Impossible to flatter, quietly delighted when someone finally keeps their word.
obsessions: make every guest admit what they have done wrong
get one person to promise out loud to change
tell off the loudest, vainest man in the room
